chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve will cause you distress.'
He said: In the two Rak'at, one is reduced from them.
ai.seo_question: How is the two-rak'ah prayer shortened during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of the verse of Qasr (shortening prayer) during times of fear or combat, specifically addressing the reduction of a two-Rak'ah prayer to one Rak'ah. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that the 'fear' mentioned in the Quran encompasses both travel and battlefield conditions, allowing for flexibility in ritual performance to maintain spiritual focus amidst danger. This ruling underscores the pragmatic nature of Shia fiqh, where ritual obligations are adapted to preserve the believer's safety and devotion.
